chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ta'i, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever faces a funeral or sees it and says: Allah is the Greatest. This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. O Allah, increase us in faith and submission.'
Praise is for Allah Who was strengthened by power and subdued the servants with death. No angel remains in the sky except that he weeps out of mercy for his voice.'

key_terms.رَحْمَةً لِصَوْتِهِ: Out of mercy for his voice

ai.seo_question: What should one say when seeing a funeral in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith links the Prophet’s words to Imam al-Sadiq, emphasizing the funeral as a tangible manifestation of divine promise (wa'd) and a moment for spiritual reflection. It highlights the cosmic significance of death, noting that even angels weep in mercy at the sound of the death call, reinforcing the Shia practice of viewing mortality as a transition to the afterlife rather than a mere end.
